activities.caption: call the daily pumping total before the calculator
activities.name: hcDailyEstimate

config.prompt: Resting heart rate ~72 beats per minute, ~70 mL per beat. Roughly how many litres does the heart move in a day?
config.why: 72 × 70 mL ≈ 5 L/min, sustained around the clock: about 7,300 litres a day through ~100,000 km of vessels. Harvey's 1628 insight was that no body could supply that hourly — so the blood must circulate.
config.context: One full circuit at rest takes about a minute, repeated roughly three billion times in a lifetime.

activities.anchor: the iron-containing protein that binds oxygen
activities.caption: file each component of the cargo by its job
activities.name: hcCargoBuckets

config.prompt: Blood is a tissue with three cell jobs — file each component:

items.label: concave discs with no nucleus, ~270 million haemoglobin molecules each
bind oxygen in the lungs, release it where concentrations fall
lymphocytes as the targeted intelligence service
cell fragments that trigger the clotting cascade
turn a leaking vessel wall into a fibrin plug within minutes

config.why: About 45% cells suspended in 55% plasma: delivery, defence and repair travelling together.

activities.caption: rebuild the conduction sequence from SA node to coronaries
activities.name: hcConductionOrder

config.prompt: One beat, in electrical order — drag the sequence into place:
items: The SA node — self-exciting cells in the right atrium — fires, roughly every 0.8 s
The excitation wave spreads through the atria, which contract and empty
The AV node relays the signal down the ventricle walls with a built-in delay
The coronary arteries, fed at the aorta's exit, fill during diastole
config.why: The delay is the design: atria finish emptying before ventricles contract. Self-excitation is why the beat persists outside the body — an electrical plant, not a metronome.

activities.anchor: bystanders learn CPR and the AED together
activities.caption: walk the two-emergencies distinction
activities.name: hcEmergencyBranch

config.root: Two cardiac emergencies that are not the same emergency.

start.text: The pump has stopped outright — no effective pulse, the person unresponsive. What is the failure mode, and what does it call for?

choices.label: Electrical failure — cardiac arrest: reset the rhythm
choices.feedback: Defibrillation addresses the rhythm while CPR maintains circulation.

choices.label: Plumbing failure — a blocked coronary artery: restore flow
choices.feedback: Restoring perfusion addresses the muscle's supply — but check what the pump itself is doing.

arrest.text: Cardiac arrest is an electrical failure: the pump has stopped, and the response is defibrillation with CPR alongside. A person can arrest even with clean arteries — an arrhythmia suffices.

plumbing.text: A heart attack is a blocked coronary artery starving the muscle; the response is restoring flow. But if the pump has stopped outright, the immediate problem is electrical — defibrillation comes first, the artery next.

attack.text: A heart attack (infarction) and cardiac arrest are distinct events: one often leads to the other, either can occur without the other, and the emergency responses differ accordingly.

config.why: Plumbing failure and electrical failure are different emergencies with different first responses — and the first-response toolkit covers both.

activities.anchor: Wave and flow are different things at different speeds
activities.caption: true or false — the pulse, read carefully
activities.name: hcPulseJudge

statements.s: The pulse you feel at the wrist is the blood itself rushing past your fingers.
statements.why: It is a pressure wave — the artery wall ballooning as systolic pressure arrives.

statements.s: The pressure wave travels along the vessel wall far faster than the blood itself moves.
statements.why: Wave and flow are different things at different speeds.

statements.s: Blood creeps through capillaries at under a millimetre per second.
statements.why: Slowed deliberately, to maximise exchange across the one-cell-thick wall.

statements.s: A pulse can be present at the wrist even when distal flow is failing.
statements.why: Which is why the wave and the flow are assessed separately at the bedside.

activities.anchor: the drainage system doubles as customs control
activities.caption: pair each lymphatic structure with its role
activities.name: hcLymphMatch

config.prompt: Drainage and defence in one network — pair each structure with its role:

pairs.right: soak up the ~3 litres of tissue fluid capillaries leak daily
one-way valves carry lymph back to the bloodstream near the collarbones
bean-shaped filters packed with lymphocytes — the immune checkpoint en route
filters blood the way nodes filter lymph, recycling worn red cells

config.why: The swollen glands of a throat infection are nodes enlarging because their immune cells are multiplying to meet the invader they have trapped.

activities.anchor: to poach oxygen across the placenta
activities.caption: fill the delivery equation and its named effect
activities.name: hcDeliveryCloze

config.text: Oxygen delivery is the product of cardiac %%0%%, haemoglobin %%1%% and saturation — about 1,000 mL O₂ per minute at rest against a ~250 mL consumption, roughly %%2%%-fold headroom. Exercising muscle, warm and CO₂-rich, shifts haemoglobin's affinity rightward and induces its own delivery: the %%3%% effect.
config.hint: Two blanks are the knobs from the slider lab; one is a number; the last is a physiologist's surname.

config.prompt: The third configuration — drag the fetal circuit's switch into order:
items: Before birth the lungs are collapsed; the placenta, not the lungs, is the exchange organ
The foramen ovale lets blood cross directly from right atrium to left
The ductus arteriosus shunts blood from the pulmonary artery into the aorta
The first breath: lung pressure falls
Both shunts close — the foramen seals into a dimple — and the adult circuit switches on
config.why: Two shunts, one switch: the double circulation read in this lesson was, for nine months, deliberately bypassed — and many congenital heart defects are that bypass failing to switch off.
